name: Honey and beetroot lip remedies

card.summary: Folk remedies using honey or beetroot juice for lip color and softness; beetroot stains temporarily, and no lip studies exist.
card.note: Honey and beet products can cause allergic reactions in some people.

quick.overview:
Honey and beetroot are used in home lip remedies. Honey is applied for moisture, beetroot juice as a natural pink-red tint.

No studies of either for changing lip color were found.
quick.mechanism: Beetroot's red pigment is betanin, a betalain used industrially as a red food colorant.[2] Honey has been studied as a wound dressing.[1]
quick.risks: Honey can interact with existing allergies according to Wikipedia, and honey is not recommended for infants under one year when eaten.[1]

lead: Honey and beetroot lip remedies are folk practices in which honey is applied to the lips for softness or beetroot juice is applied for a pink or red tint.

Beetroot owes its red color to betanin, which is used commercially as a red food colorant.[2] Honey has antibacterial activity in laboratory settings and preliminary evidence suggests faster healing of partial-thickness burns, but these findings concern wound care, not lip color.[1]
No published study of either substance for lip appearance was identified.

paras: Honey is a long-standing folk treatment for burns and skin injuries. Evidence for most wound uses is low quality, and the FDA has approved several medical-grade honey products for minor wounds and burns.[1]
Betanin is the red pigment in beetroot and is used in foods such as sauces, desserts and candy.[2] Eating beetroot can turn urine or stool reddish, which is harmless.[2]
Lips have thin tissue and no sweat glands, so they dry and chap easily.[3] Natural lip color depends on blood visible through thin tissue and on melanin content.[3]
